Topic 01
Code review agents & harness
Subagents that review, an adversary that tries to break the change, and a skill that runs them both.
Day 2 · Code review agents · 03
The idea
A review harness in one picture
/review-pr 482
The skill runs in your main session
format-reviewer
file-reviewer
connection-reviewer
coverage-reviewer
Adversary
Proves or drops every finding
Report generator
Same template, every time
A skill starts four focused reviewers in parallel, an adversary checks their work, and a report generator writes one report in a fixed format.
Day 2 · Code review agents · 04
Split the review
Four lenses, four small agents
1 · Format
Style, naming, lint, import order, dead code and debug logs.
2 · Files
Right files changed, nothing missing, each file correct on its own.
3 · Cross-connections
Callers, types, APIs, configs and other packages outside the diff.
4 · Test coverage
Every changed path has a test that would fail if it broke.
Day 2 · Code review agents · 05
How to build one
A review agent in four steps
1
One lens
One question. "Is the format right?" beats "Is it good?"
2
Read-only tools
Read, Grep, Glob, Bash. No Edit, so it can only report.
3
A short checklist
Five lines it can tick off. Point to CLAUDE.md, don't copy it.
4
Fixed output
Same format for every agent, so the report generator can merge them.
Start with /agents → Create new agent, let Claude draft it, then trim it to these four parts. Save it in .claude/agents/ so the team shares it.
Day 2 · Code review agents · 06
Agent 1 of 4
format-reviewer: is it written our way?
Mechanical checks, so a small fast model is enough.
Runs the real linter, not an opinion
Ignores logic on purpose
.claude/agents/format-reviewer.md
---
name: format-reviewer
description: Checks a diff against our style and naming rules.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
model: haiku
---
Check format only. Ignore logic.
1. Run git diff --name-only main...HEAD
2. Run npm run lint on those files
3. Check naming, import order and file layout against
   the Code style section of CLAUDE.md
4. Flag dead code, console.log and TODOs without a ticket
Report: SEVERITY · FORMAT · file:line · finding · fix
Day 2 · Code review agents · 07
Agent 2 of 4
file-reviewer: are the right files right?
Looks at the set of files first, then each file on its own.
Catches the missing test or migration
Catches .env and debug files sneaking in
.claude/agents/file-reviewer.md
---
name: file-reviewer
description: Checks the changed files: complete, correct, clean.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
model: sonnet
---
The set: is anything missing or unexpected?
- New logic without a test file, schema without a migration
- .env, secrets, lockfile or generated files committed
Each file on its own:
- Logic errors, unhandled null and errors, leftover mocks
- In the right folder for its role?
Report: SEVERITY · FILES · file:line · finding · fix
Day 2 · Code review agents · 08
Agent 3 of 4
connection-reviewer: what else does it touch?
The bugs a diff hides live outside the diff. This agent goes looking.
Greps every caller of what changed
Checks the other packages in a monorepo
.claude/agents/connection-reviewer.md
---
name: connection-reviewer
description: Checks how a change connects to the rest of the code.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
model: opus
---
Look beyond the diff. For every changed export:
1. Grep every caller. Does each one still work?
2. Changed a type, API or DB column? Check all consumers:
   frontend, backend, app, jobs, tests
3. Routes, config and env vars still in sync?
4. Any new circular import?
Report: SEVERITY · CONNECT · file:line · finding · fix
Day 2 · Code review agents · 09
Agent 4 of 4
coverage-reviewer: would a test catch it?
Coverage numbers alone lie. This agent checks that tests actually exercise the change.
Only the changed code, not the whole repo
Missing error-path tests are the usual find
.claude/agents/coverage-reviewer.md
---
name: coverage-reviewer
description: Checks that the changed code is covered by tests.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
model: sonnet
---
Check coverage for the changed code only.
1. Run npm test -- --coverage --changedSince=main
2. For each changed function: is there a test that
   fails if it breaks? A line hit is not enough.
3. Flag untested branches: errors, empty input, retries
4. New code below our threshold (e.g. 80%) = RISK
Report: SEVERITY · COVERAGE · file:line · finding · fix
Day 2 · Code review agents · 10
Real example
The adversary checks the checkers
It gets the diff plus the four reports. Every claim needs proof.
A failing test turns an opinion into evidence
False positives are dropped, with a reason
.claude/agents/adversarial-reviewer.md
---
name: adversarial-reviewer
description: Challenges review findings and the change itself.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash
model: opus
---
You get the diff and four review reports.
1. For each finding: prove it with a failing test or
   a trace, or mark it FALSE POSITIVE with the reason.
2. Assume the change is still wrong. What did all four
   miss? Edge cases, races, silent data loss.
3. Pass on only CONFIRMED and NEW findings (lens ADVERSARY
   for new ones), plus the count of false positives.
Day 2 · Code review agents · 11
The report generator
report-generator: same report, every time
Its only job is formatting. The template lives in the skill folder, so the format never drifts.
Cheap model, strict template
Saved to reviews/ so you can compare PRs
.claude/agents/report-generator.md
---
name: report-generator
description: Writes the PR review report in our fixed format.
tools: Read, Write
model: haiku
---
Input: the confirmed findings from adversarial-reviewer.
1. Read .claude/skills/review-pr/report-template.md
2. Fill it in exactly. Same headings, same columns, same order.
3. Never add, drop or reword findings. Never add prose.
4. Status is BLOCKED if any BLOCKER, else READY.
5. Save to reviews/pr-<number>.md and return the report.

Day 2 · Code review agents · 13
Skill + subagents, for real
A real gate: three reviewers at once
1
The builder finishes
A general-purpose subagent builds sub-plan 2.12. It ran for 1h 3m on its own.
2
The gate fans out
design-guardian, test-guardian and agent-skills:code-reviewer start in the background, in parallel.
3
Then plan sync
Only when all 3 return does the main session update the plan.
Main context stays at 17%. Each reviewer spends its own ~120–150k tokens.
Day 2 · Code review agents · 14
The skill
One command runs the whole review
The skill is the recipe: fetch, fan out, challenge, format.
Four reviewers run in parallel
Manual only, never posts on its own
.claude/skills/review-pr/SKILL.md
---
name: review-pr
description: Multi-agent review of a pull request
argument-hint: [pr-number]
disable-model-invocation: true
---
1. Run gh pr diff $ARGUMENTS > /tmp/pr-$ARGUMENTS.diff
2. In parallel, run format-reviewer, file-reviewer,
   connection-reviewer and coverage-reviewer on that diff
3. Give the diff and all four reports to adversarial-reviewer
4. Give its output to report-generator
5. Show me the report as-is. Never post it without asking.

Topic 02
Monorepo: one central Claude
Frontend, backend and app in one repo. Each gets its own guide, and a root that keeps them in line.
Day 2 · Monorepo · 18
The problem
Three stacks, one Claude
In a monorepo Claude must know which rules apply where. A React rule in backend/ is noise. A DB rule in app/ is wrong.
Each folder needs its own guidance
Cross-folder changes need a plan first
Shared agents avoid copy-paste setups

Day 2 · Monorepo · 20
Folder layout
Where each piece lives
All agents sit in the root .claude/ so every Orca worktree session can find them. Each package keeps its own CLAUDE.md and plans/.
Launch Claude from the repo root
Package CLAUDE.md loads when Claude reads that folder
repo/
repo/
├── CLAUDE.md # root router + shared rules
├── .claude/
│ ├── agents/
│ │ ├── *-reviewer.md # the review agents
│ │ └── planner.md # shared, planning only
│ ├── hooks/only-plans.sh
│ └── skills/plan-feature/SKILL.md
├── frontend/ CLAUDE.md · plans/
├── backend/ CLAUDE.md · plans/
└── app/ CLAUDE.md · plans/
Day 2 · Monorepo · 21
Root CLAUDE.md
The root guide is a map, not a manual
Short. It tells Claude where things are and the rules every package shares.
"MUST" for rules that are never optional
Details stay in each package's CLAUDE.md
CLAUDE.md
# Monorepo map
- frontend/ web client → read frontend/CLAUDE.md first
- backend/ API + DB → read backend/CLAUDE.md first
- app/ mobile app → read app/CLAUDE.md first
 
# Rules
- MUST follow the CLAUDE.md of every folder you touch
- One package per task. Cross-package = plan first
- Plans live in <package>/plans/<ticket>.md, never root
Day 2 · Monorepo · 22
Planning only
Shared agents plan. Each package builds.
Ticket
SHOP-231: add gift cards
/plan-feature
Finds the packages it touches
planner
Read-only on code. Writes plans only.
frontend/plans/SHOP-231.md
backend/plans/SHOP-231.md
One plan per folder, each written against that folder's CLAUDE.md. Then each package's Claude Code session in Orca ADE builds its own plan.
Day 2 · Monorepo · 23
Real example
The planner can only write plans
It gets Write, but a hook in its frontmatter blocks any path outside plans/.
Hook runs only while this agent is active
Opus for planning, cheaper models to build
.claude/agents/planner.md
---
name: planner
description: Writes implementation plans. Never edits source.
tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Write
model: opus
hooks:
  PreToolUse:
    - matcher: "Write"
      hooks:
        - type: command
          command: "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/only-plans.sh"
---
Read <package>/CLAUDE.md, then write <package>/plans/<ticket>.md
Day 2 · Monorepo · 24
Real example
A skill that must follow folder guidance
One command plans a ticket across every package it touches.
Folder CLAUDE.md is read before planning
Stops before any code is written
.claude/skills/plan-feature/SKILL.md
---
name: plan-feature
description: Plan a ticket across packages, one plan per folder
argument-hint: [ticket-id]
---
1. Work out which packages ticket $ARGUMENTS touches.
2. For each package, read its CLAUDE.md first.
3. Use the planner agent to write <package>/plans/$ARGUMENTS.md
4. Each plan MUST follow its folder's CLAUDE.md.
5. List the plans and wait. No code in this skill.

Topic 03
Let Claude see the browser
Two tools that close the loop on UI work: Chrome DevTools MCP and Playwright CLI.
Day 2 · Browser tools · 26
Two tools, two jobs
Debug the page, or drive the flow
Chrome DevTools MCP
Best for: why a page is slow or broken.
How: performance traces, network, console, screenshots.
"Why is checkout slow?"
Playwright CLI
Best for: checking that a flow works, cheaply.
How: short commands. Snapshots go to disk, not into context.
"Does sign-up still work?"
Day 2 · Browser tools · 27
Chrome DevTools MCP
Give Claude real DevTools
Claude opens Chrome, records a trace, reads network and console, and reports back.
install
claude mcp add chrome-devtools --scope user \
  npx chrome-devtools-mcp@latest
Try: Open localhost:3000/checkout, record a performance trace and tell me what slows down LCP. Check the console too.
Day 2 · Browser tools · 28
Playwright CLI
Browser automation that saves tokens
install
npm install -g @playwright/cli@latest
playwright-cli install --skills
what Claude runs
playwright-cli open localhost:3000 --headed
playwright-cli type "Buy groceries"
playwright-cli press Enter
playwright-cli screenshot
Compact commands instead of a full page tree in every reply.
--skills teaches Claude the commands
Good fit for our browser-tester agent
Try: Use playwright-cli to test the add-todo flow. Screenshot every passing and failing step.

Topic 04
Practical takeaways
What actually moves the needle: a lean setup, clear specs, careful review and habits Claude can follow.
Day 2 · Takeaways · 30
In one slide
Four things worth keeping
Keep your setup lean
Every skill, MCP server and CLAUDE.md line costs context. Keep what you use.
Measure before you trust
Try a "must-install" tip on one real task. Keep it only if results improve.
Invest in specs and review
Clear specs in, careful review out. That is where your time pays off.
Stay portable
AGENTS.md plus a fallback harness, so an outage or price change never stalls you.

Day 2 · Takeaways · 32
Guideline 1
Give Claude a way to verify its work
Test cases
Give inputs and expected outputs. Ask it to run the tests.
Verify the UI
Screenshot the result and compare it with the design.
Root cause, not symptoms
Ask for the fix and the proof. No silenced errors.
Day 2 · Takeaways · 33
Guideline 2
Explore first, then plan, then code
1
Explore
Plan mode (Shift+Tab). Claude reads files and answers questions. No edits.
2
Plan
Ask for a written plan. Ctrl+G opens it in your editor to adjust.
3
Code
Back to normal mode. Build against the plan and verify.
Skip the plan when you can describe the whole diff in one sentence.
Day 2 · Takeaways · 34
Guideline 3
Give specific context in your prompts
Scope it
Which file, which scenario, what is out of scope.
Point to the source
"Check git log for how this API changed."
Reference a pattern
"Follow @src/api/client.ts."
Describe the symptom
What you saw, where, and when it happens.
Paste an image
Designs, screenshots, error dialogs.
Configure permissions
Allow safe commands so it doesn't stop to ask.
Day 2 · Takeaways · 35
Permissions and hooks
Allow the safe, block the risky, automate the boring
Stop approving the same command twenty times, and never let Claude read secrets.
allow: commands you always approve
deny: secrets and irreversible actions
hooks: things that must happen every time
.claude/settings.json
{
  "permissions": {
    "allow": ["Bash(npm run test:*)", "Bash(gh pr view:*)"],
    "deny": ["Read(./.env)", "Bash(git push:*)"]
  },
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [{
      "matcher": "Edit|Write",
      "hooks": [{ "type": "command",
                  "command": ".claude/hooks/format.sh" }]
    }]
  }
}

Day 2 · Takeaways · 38
AskUserQuestion
Let Claude interview you
Claude asks multiple-choice questions and you pick answers. Great before a spec or a plan, when you haven't thought of every edge case.
Try: I want bulk export in the admin panel. Interview me with the AskUserQuestion tool about scope, formats and edge cases, then write the spec to specs/bulk-export.md.
Day 2 · Takeaways · 39
Esc + Esc or /rewind
Rewind instead of arguing
You: add refresh
Claude edits 3 files
You: add retries
Auth breaks
Restore code and conversation
Back to the moment before it went wrong.
Restore conversation
Keep the code, rewind the chat.
Restore code
Keep the chat, undo the edits.
Summarize from here
Compress everything after that message.
Checkpoints track Claude's file edits, not side effects of bash commands like migrations or deploys.
Day 2 · Takeaways · 40
CLAUDE.md
What belongs in CLAUDE.md
Keep
Code style that differs from defaults
Gotchas and non-obvious behaviour
Repo etiquette: branches, PRs
Architecture decisions for this project
Bash commands Claude can't guess
Leave out
Anything it can learn from the code
Standard language conventions
File-by-file tours of the codebase
"Write clean code" and other truisms
Detailed API docs (link instead)
